decision: Does the OSS 'cupy drop-in, no kernel fusion' practice (array-API swap only) transfer to TensorLBM's PyTorch stack, i.e. does a single SOY free-energy D2Q9 implementation driven through two array backends reproduce (a) the executed OSS reference numbers and (b) the analytic Young-Laplace law within the owner precision standard?
alternatives: A: array-API drop-in (NumPy <-> PyTorch eager), one implementation, no custom/fused kernels (the OSS practice).
B: hand-written fused kernels per backend (out of scope for this mission; noted as the alternative the OSS project also declined).
hypothesis: H1: the TensorLBM port reproduces the analytic Laplace jump dp = sigma/R within 15 % (owner standard); H2: the two TensorLBM backends agree to < 1e-6 relative on dp (true drop-in equivalence, not just 'similar results'); H3: the executed OSS reference code agrees with the TensorLBM port to within a few percent on dp, the residual being boundary-ghost and initialisation choices.
unit_of_analysis: one simulation (one radius, one parameter set, one arm), outcome = measured Laplace pressure jump dp between droplet interior and exterior.
metric: dp = mean(p | r < R - xi) - mean(p | r > R + xi), p = rho/3 + psi*mu; error = 100*(dp - sigma/R)/(sigma/R) [%].
secondary_metrics: u_max residual velocity at the sampling step (steadiness indicator)
sigma from capillary energy: sigma_cap = sum(kappa*|grad psi|^2) / (2*pi*R), reported as an independent surface-tension route
array ops per step and wall time per step (cost of the no-fusion practice)

thresholds.notes: 15 % is the owner precision standard for cross-validation; the backend-agreement criterion is the drop-in-equivalence definition (same algorithm, different array namespace).

stopping_rule: Fixed step budget (2000 lattice steps, dp sampled every 100 steps); no step count is extended after seeing the result. A case whose sampled dp band crosses the +-15 % band is reported as a band, not as the best sample.

repetitions.rationale: Fully deterministic: no random seeds, no stochastic collision, no wall-clock-dependent logic. Repeat runs of the same configuration differ only by floating-point summation order; the auditor's independent re-run of the previous round reproduced dp bit-for-bit (6.671389e-04). Variation is therefore explored through the parameter sweeps below, not through repetitions.

controlled: same D2Q9 constants and update order
confounders: initial interface width (a 2x-too-sharp initial tanh relaxes slowly and biases dp by tens of percent; swept explicitly)
initial transient vs sampling step (dp oscillates before settling; the full dp(t) band is reported)

OSS reference ghosts: the OSS source hard-codes +1/-1 ghost columns for its Zou-He inlet/outlet, which is inconsistent with a periodic droplet box; the adapter sets them to the far-field value -1 and the resulting agreement is reported rather than hidden
float64 vs float32: only float64 used, so no dtype confound

convergence.expectation: error should shrink as R/xi grows (diffuse-interface curvature correction ~ O(xi/R))

environment.device: CPU (torch CUDA not used; the drop-in claim is tested through the eager CPU path, GPU is a device swap)
environment.oss_reference: ebinan92/Fingering_dynamics @ 150a573, lattice_boltzmann/fingering_periodic.py, read-only checkout (OSS_FINGERING_ROOT), executed not vendored

analysis_plan.aggregation: per-arm final dp at the fixed step budget, plus the full sampled history
analysis_plan.uncertainty: reported as the min/max of the sampled dp band over the last third of the run
analysis_plan.outliers: none removed; non-finite results are reported as failures with the failing step
analysis_plan.acceptance: H1 and H2 are pass/fail machine checks; H3 is reported as a number with the boundary/initialisation caveat

limitations: Periodic domain only: the OSS Zou-He inlet/outlet and half-way bounce-back walls are not exercised.
GPU/CuPy path is not executed on this host (no GPU); the practice is validated through the array-API-swap equivalence rather than through CuPy itself.

The Laplace law is an analytic reference, not an experimental measurement; sigma is the model surface tension implied by kappa = 0.75*sigma*xi (self-consistent, cross-checked with the capillary-energy route).
